title: app-provisioner-one-owner

test_results.outcome: exit 0: 'Application Plane audit stream contract: ok (5 subjects, 2 durables, 2 publishers)'

residual_risks: Not verified against a live nats-box: the JSON keys max_age, max_msgs, ack_wait and max_deliver (in nanoseconds) and the `stream edit` / `consumer edit ... --max-deliver=5 --wait=30s --force` flags. If a key does not match, the scripts print '~' and edit on every run. That does no harm but is noisy. The lead should check the first live run shows '~' once for each of the four shared durables and then '=' on a rerun.

The brief said notification-core-conversation-followed-message is created only by the Go provisioner, but the host script already created it at HEAD. The coder kept it and gave it the shared values (30 s / 5). This matches audit-core, so Control will accept it. The container entrypoint still does not create it, as before.

The scripts converge only max_age/max_msgs (streams) and max_deliver/ack_wait (consumers). Mismatches in other ensureFixedConsumer fields (deliver subject/group, filter, deliver/ack/replay policy) are not converged. The contract test pins the filter and delivery subjects in both scripts, so they match on creation. A durable that already exists with a different filter would still be refused by Control, and that would need an owner decision.
Go's ensureRuntimeStream passes MaxBytes 0 while the scripts create with --max-bytes=-1. The server normalizes 0 to -1, so no drift is expected, but this was not confirmed live.

If `stream info --json` / `consumer info --json` fails, json_has falls through to an edit instead of failing. This is harmless because the edit is non-destructive, and under set -e / explicit exit 1 a failed edit still exits non-zero.
deploy_notes: Live proof for the lead: after the Control run, expect '=' for the three runtime streams (already 336 h / 1,000,000), '~' once for each of the four shared durables (max-deliver -1 to 5), then all '=' on a rerun. Control's audit-extra provisioner should then accept those durables. NOT verified against a live nats-box: the JSON keys (max_age, max_msgs, ack_wait, max_deliver in nanoseconds) and the stream edit / consumer edit flags exactly as the packet gives them. If a key does not match, the scripts converge every run instead of skipping. That is harmless but prints '~' each time, so check the first live run. Owner decisions: (1) notification-core-conversation-followed-message. The packet says only the Go provisioner creates it, but scripts/provision-jetstream.sh also creates it with the default max-deliver -1, and Control refuses that. I gave it the shared values (a deliberate deviation). The alternative is to remove it from the host script. (2) Runtime streams move from 72 h to 336 h retention (audit-core's value). Confirm this is acceptable under zero data retention for any content those events carry. (3) Converging max-msgs to 1,000,000 discards the oldest messages beyond the cap on any stream holding more (live counts are far lower, per the packet). (4) Host script failures now exit 1. Before, a failed add was silently skipped by the '&& echo' pattern. Notes: the packet's computed task text listed no files, but its JSON record names the three scripts above, so I followed the JSON. The leads-core publisher.go and sync.go show as modified in this worktree; another packet made those edits and I did not touch them. It is offline and reads the repo scripts.
summary: Both Application Plane provisioners now create and converge the three runtime streams (VEREVON_APPLICATION, VEREVON_INGESTION, VEREVON_MODEL) to audit-core's 336 h / 1,000,000 values, using stream edit when they differ. The contract test now pins the runtime streams and shared durables against provisioner.go in both scripts.
